headline: Chubb Re-Energized, CJGJ Pays Off Staffer's Loans
writeup: Buffalo Bills training camp's first week was headlined by a frightening moment on Day 3 when new safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson was carted off with what was later diagnosed as a lower calf strain, though subsequent updates offered cautious optimism that he may avoid the worst-case scenario. Off the field, Gardner-Johnson further endeared himself to the organization by paying off $20,000 in student loans for a Bills camp staffer, while his teammates and coaches praised his passionate, edge-bringing presence on the defense. Bradley Chubb emerged as a camp standout, declaring that joining Buffalo has re-energized his career, with observers noting he looks like the pass-rush difference-maker the Bills have been seeking since 2019. Rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr turned heads and second-round cornerback Maxwell Hairston found himself in a heated position battle, while wide receivers Joshua Palmer and newly signed DJ Moore drew attention as potential offensive surprises alongside a rejuvenated Tyler Bass. The week also brought roster moves including the signing of CB D.J. Miller, injury concerns for WR Dante Pettis, broader questions about first-team roster openings and stadium affordability, a heartwarming community moment as the Bills honored Monroe HS, and a look at HC Joe Brady leaving the door open for a Stefon Diggs reunion while Jim Leonhard expressed awe at the team's football culture.
